issue_context.title: Route level hooks validation
issue_context.body:
<!--
Before you submit an issue we recommend you visit [Fastify Help](https://github.com/fastify/help) and ask any questions you have or mention any problems you've had getting started with Fastify.

**Please read this entire template before posting any issue. If you ignore these instructions
and post an issue here that does not follow the instructions, your issue might be closed,
locked, and assigned the `missing discussion` label.**
-->

## 🐛 Bug Report

Fastify currently doesn't validate route-level hooks:
- Property name typos go unnoticed
- Hooks can both be async and use done callback

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

```js
const fastify = require('fastify')({
  logger: true
})


fastify.addHook('preHandler', (request, reply, done) => {
  console.log('inside shared preHandler')
  done()
})

fastify.route({
  method: 'GET',
  url: '/',
  // Property name typo, hook not called
  preHandlre: function (request, reply, done) {
    console.log('inside route preHandler')
    done()
  },
  preValidation: async function (request, reply, done) {
    console.log('inside route preValidation (using both async and done callback)')
    done()
  },
  handler: function (request, reply) {
    console.log('inside handler')
    setTimeout(() => reply.send({ hello: 'world' }), 1000)
  }
})

fastify.listen(3000, (err, address) => {
  if (err) throw err
  fastify.log.info(`server listening on ${address}`)
})

```

## Output

```
❯ node typo.js 
{"level":30,"time":1611921669902,"pid":19370,"hostname":"macbook.local","msg":"Server listening at http://127.0.0.1:3000"}
{"level":30,"time":1611921669903,"pid":19370,"hostname":"macbook.local","msg":"server listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000"}
{"level":30,"time":1611921671922,"pid":19370,"hostname":"macbook.local","reqId":1,"req":{"method":"GET","url":"/","hostname":"127.0.0.1:3000","remoteAddress":"127.0.0.1","remotePort":51239},"msg":"incoming request"}
inside route preValidation (using both async and done callback)
inside shared preHandler
inside handler
inside shared preHandler
inside handler
{"level":30,"time":1611921672929,"pid":19370,"hostname":"macbook.local","reqId":1,"res":{"statusCode":200},"responseTime":1006.7353990077972,"msg":"request completed"}
{"level":40,"time":1611921672930,"pid":19370,"hostname":"macbook.local","reqId":1,"err":{"type":"FastifyError","message":"Reply was already sent.","stack":"FastifyError: Reply was already sent.\n    at _Reply.Reply.send (/Users/ayoub/Universe/upwork/gadget/fastify/lib/reply.js:113:26)\n    at Timeout._onTimeout (/Users/ayoub/Universe/upwork/gadget/fastify/typo.js:23:28)\n    at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:556:17)\n    at processTimers (node:internal/timers:499:7)","name":"FastifyError","code":"FST_ERR_REP_ALREADY_SENT","statusCode":500},"msg":"Reply already sent"}
```

## Expected behavior
Regarding the use of both async/done, I would expect fastify to validate route level hooks the same way it does for shared hooks added using `fastify.addHook()`.

Regarding incorrect hook property names, I'm not sure how we should proceed with that but I believe it should be handled somehow. Maybe wrap all route-level hooks in the route definition inside an object to be able to loop through them and validate?

## Your Environment

- *node version*: 15.2.1
- *fastify version*: 3.9.2
- *os*: Mac
comments:
I'm not convinced we should validate the options as it allows other plugin developers to add their custom options. I agree that this is a problem - maybe adding a `hooks` prefix is right approach, would you mind sending a PR? I would recommend we don't remove the current behavior.

(note that your prevalidation hook is wrong, it has both async and a callback).
> I'm not convinced we should validate the options as it allows other plugin developers to add their custom options. I agree that this is a problem - maybe adding a `hooks` prefix is right approach, would you mind sending a PR? I would recommend we don't remove the current behavior.

Will send a PR.

> (note that your prevalidation hook is wrong, it has both async and a callback).

Yes I explicitly used both since that is also an issue I believe. Users sometimes [make the mistake of using both](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-postgres/issues/74).
We already validate the hook params [when added using](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/fastify.js#L461-L473
) `fastify.addHook()`, I think we should do so for route-level hooks as well.

review_comments: I'd add a comment above this switch to explain why the `fn.length` is being inspected.

Will do, thanks!

Had a lot on my plate for the past few weeks, will get around to this during the next week.

I'm still gonna change this property name to something fastify specific because of potential collisions, otherwise if some potential user with a custom plugin that uses a `hooks` property as a route-level option, his hooks might end up being skipped.

Suggestions welcome!
